options.text: A basket of summer fruit
A plumb line
Locusts devouring the land
Fire consuming the land

questions.explanation: In Amos 7:1-9, Amos has a series of visions. The third vision is of a plumb line, which symbolizes God's judgment on Israel for their deviation from righteousness. The correct answer is 'A plumb line.'

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.question_text: In the diagram below, a map illustrates Paul's missionary journeys. In the context of Acts 16:11-15, what is the significance of Philippi during Paul's second missionary journey?
questions.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><path d='M100,100 L150,150' stroke='black'/></svg>

options.text: It was the first European city Paul preached in.
It was where Paul encountered significant opposition.
It was a major center for early Christianity.
It was where Lydia, a seller of purple fabrics, was converted.

questions.explanation: According to Acts 16:11-15, during Paul's second missionary journey, he preached in Philippi, where Lydia, a seller of purple fabrics, was converted. This event is significant as it marks one of the early conversions in Europe. Thus, the correct answer is related to Lydia's conversion.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.subtopic: Sermon on the Mount and Parables
questions.question_text: In the Parable of the Sower (Matthew 13:1-23), what does the seed that falls on rocky ground represent?

options.text: Those who hear the word and understand it.
Those who hear the word but are choked by worldly cares.
Those who hear the word but lack depth, falling away when trials come.
Those who hear the word and produce a bountiful harvest.

questions.explanation: In the Parable of the Sower (Matthew 13:1-23), the seed that falls on rocky ground represents those who hear the word but lack depth and fall away when trials come. This explanation is given by Jesus Himself in Matthew 13:20-21.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: According to Joshua 24:1-28, what was the significance of the covenant renewal ceremony at Shechem?

options.text: It marked the beginning of Joshua's leadership.
It was a ceremony to consecrate the new temple.
It was a reaffirmation of Israel's commitment to God's laws.
It signified the end of the conquest of Canaan.

questions.explanation: The covenant renewal ceremony at Shechem, as described in Joshua 24:1-28, was significant because it involved a reaffirmation of Israel's commitment to God's laws. Joshua gathered the tribes and reminded them of God's faithfulness, urging them to serve the Lord faithfully. This ceremony reinforced their covenant with God.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 9:1-8, Jesus heals a paralytic man. What is Jesus' initial response to the man?

options.text: Your sins are forgiven
Rise and walk
Follow me
Go and sin no more

questions.explanation: According to Matthew 9:2, Jesus tells the paralytic man, 'Take heart, son; your sins are forgiven.' This response indicates Jesus' authority to forgive sins, which was a significant aspect of His ministry.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: According to Joshua 8:1-29, what was the outcome of Joshua's strategy at Ai?
questions.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='50' y='50' width='100' height='50' fill='#ccc'/><text x='100' y='80' font-size='24'>Ai</text></svg>

options.text: The city was captured on the first attempt
The city was captured using an ambush strategy
The city was not captured and Joshua retreated
The city was captured without any battle

questions.explanation: Joshua 8:1-29 describes how Joshua used an ambush strategy to capture Ai after an initial defeat. The strategy involved a main force and a hidden ambush that attacked Ai from behind, leading to its capture.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.question_text: According to Acts 16:16-24, what was the outcome for Paul and Silas after they cast out a spirit from a slave girl?

options.text: They were praised by the slave girl's owners
They were beaten and imprisoned
They were asked to leave the city
They were ignored by the crowd

questions.explanation: Acts 16:16-24 records that after Paul cast out the spirit, he and Silas were beaten and imprisoned by the authorities because their actions were seen as disturbing the peace and promoting practices not acceptable to the Romans.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.subtopic: Sermon on the Mount and Parables
questions.question_text: In the Parable of the Talents (Matthew 25:14-30), what is the fate of the servant who received one talent?

options.text: He is praised for his faithfulness
He is cast into outer darkness
He is given more talents
He is forgiven for his lack of action

questions.explanation: According to Matthew 25:24-30, the servant who received one talent is described as wicked and lazy because he did not invest the talent. As a result, he is cast into outer darkness where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: In Amos 9:11-15, what does Amos prophesy regarding Israel's future?

options.text: Complete destruction and exile
Restoration and rebuilding
Continued judgment and punishment
No change in their current state

questions.explanation: Amos 9:11-15 prophesies a future restoration for Israel, where God will rebuild the fallen booth of David, repair its damages, and plant them firmly in their land, never to be uprooted again.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 9:32-34, Jesus heals a man who was demon-possessed and mute. What was the reaction of the Pharisees to this miracle?

options.text: They praised Jesus for His divine power
They were amazed and believed in Jesus
They attributed Jesus' power to Beelzebub, the prince of demons
They remained silent and indifferent

questions.explanation: According to Matthew 9:32-34, after Jesus heals the demon-possessed mute man, the Pharisees react by saying, 'It is by the prince of demons that this fellow drives out demons.' This indicates they attributed Jesus' miraculous power to Beelzebub, showing their skepticism and hostility towards Jesus.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: In Amos 7:10-17, what is Amaziah's response to Amos' prophecy against Jeroboam and Israel?

options.text: He repents and asks for forgiveness
He accuses Amos of treason and advises him to flee to Judah
He ignores Amos and continues with the religious rituals
He asks Amos to pray for Israel's restoration

questions.explanation: Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, responds to Amos by accusing him of conspiracy against King Jeroboam and advising him to flee to Judah to prophesy and earn his living there, indicating Amaziah's attempt to suppress Amos' prophecy and send him away.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.question_text: According to Acts 16:25-34, what is the immediate result of Paul and Silas praying and singing hymns to God in prison?

options.text: The prison doors remained locked, and they were not freed
An earthquake occurred, and the prison doors were opened
The jailer was angered and wanted to punish them further
Paul and Silas were transferred to a different prison

questions.explanation: Acts 16:25-34 describes that as Paul and Silas prayed and sang hymns, an earthquake occurred, opening the prison doors and unshackling their chains. This event leads to the jailer's conversion after he and his household are baptized.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.subtopic: Sermon on the Mount and Parables
questions.question_text: In the Parable of the Talents (Matthew 25:14-30), what does the master commend the servants for who invested their talents wisely?

options.text: Their ability to hide their talents safely
Their decision to trade and multiply their talents
Their loyalty in serving the master directly
Their fear of the master's return

questions.explanation: In the Parable of the Talents, the master commends the servants who received talents and invested them wisely, resulting in a profit. This is seen in Matthew 25:14-30, where the servants who doubled their talents are praised and rewarded.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: In the diagram below, a map illustrates the conquest of Canaan under Joshua. In the context of Joshua 6:1-27, what is the significance of the fall of Jericho?
questions.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='10' width='300' height='180' fill='none' stroke='black'/><text x='160' y='100' text-anchor='middle'>Map of Canaan</text></svg>

options.text: It marked the beginning of Israel's conquest of Canaan
It was the final city to be conquered before dividing the land
It demonstrated God's power and Israel's faith in following His instructions
It was a victory achieved solely through Israel's military strength

questions.explanation: The fall of Jericho, as described in Joshua 6:1-27, is significant because it demonstrates God's miraculous power and Israel's obedience to His instructions. The city's walls fell after the Israelites marched around it for seven days, following God's command, showcasing divine intervention.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 9:20-22, a woman with a bleeding disorder touches Jesus' garment. What is Jesus' response to the woman?

options.text: He ignores her and continues on His way.
He rebukes her for touching Him.
He turns and says, 'Daughter, your faith has healed you.'
He asks who touched Him and then heals her.

questions.explanation: According to Matthew 9:20-22, when the woman with a bleeding disorder touches Jesus' garment, Jesus turns and says, 'Daughter, your faith has healed you.' This response indicates Jesus' awareness of the miracle and His affirmation of the woman's faith.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: In Amos 7:1-9, what is the content of Amos' third vision?

options.text: A basket of summer fruit
A plumb line
A swarm of locusts
Fire that devours the land

questions.explanation: Amos 7:7-9 describes Amos' third vision as seeing the Lord standing by a wall that had been built with a plumb line, and He had a plumb line in His hand. This vision symbolizes God's judgment on Israel for their deviation from righteousness.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.question_text: In the diagram below, a map illustrates Paul's second missionary journey. In the context of Acts 16:11-15, what is the significance of Philippi?
questions.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><path d='M100,100 L150,150' stroke='black'/></svg>

options.text: It was the first European city Paul preached in.
It was a major Jewish center where Paul faced opposition.
Paul received a vision to go to Macedonia there.
It was the final destination of his second journey.

questions.explanation: Acts 16:11-15 describes Paul's ministry in Philippi, noting it as a significant stop on his second missionary journey. Philippi is highlighted as the first European city Paul preached in, marking the beginning of Christianity in Europe.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.subtopic: Sermon on the Mount and Parables
questions.question_text: In the Parable of the Talents (Matthew 25:14-30), what does the master commend the servants for who invested their talents?

options.text: For being cautious and not risking their talents.
For their faithfulness in using their talents wisely.
For hiding their talents to avoid loss.
For returning the exact amount they received.

questions.explanation: The Parable of the Talents in Matthew 25:14-30 commends the servants who invested their talents and generated a return. The master's commendation is based on their faithfulness and initiative in using their talents wisely, demonstrating a positive and productive stewardship.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: According to Joshua 8:1-29, what was the outcome of Joshua's strategy at Ai?

options.text: The Israelites were defeated due to Achan's sin.
The city was captured through an ambush and subsequent attack.
Joshua directly assaulted the city and was victorious.
The city was spared due to the inhabitants' repentance.

questions.explanation: Joshua 8:1-29 describes the Israelites' victory at Ai through a clever strategy involving an ambush. Joshua's plan included setting an ambush behind the city, which then attacked Ai from the rear while Joshua feigned a retreat, leading to the capture of the city.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.subtopic: Sermon on the Mount and Parables
questions.question_text: In the Parable of the Mustard Seed (Matthew 13:31-32), what does Jesus compare the Kingdom of Heaven to?

options.text: A grain of wheat
A mustard seed
A pearl of great price
A treasure hidden in a field

questions.explanation: The Parable of the Mustard Seed is found in Matthew 13:31-32. Jesus compares the Kingdom of Heaven to a mustard seed, which is small but grows into a large tree. This parable illustrates the growth of the Kingdom from small beginnings to something significant.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: According to Joshua 10:1-27, what was the significance of the sun standing still during Joshua's battle against the Amorites?

options.text: It signified the end of the day
It allowed the Israelites more time to fight
It was a sign of God's displeasure
It marked the beginning of a new era

questions.explanation: In Joshua 10:1-27, the sun standing still allowed the Israelites more time to complete their victory over the Amorites, demonstrating God's intervention on their behalf.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.question_text: In the diagram below, a map illustrates Paul's first missionary journey. In the context of Acts 13:4-12, what is the significance of Paul's encounter with Elymas the magician on the island of Cyprus? In the diagram below, ...
questions.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><path d='M10 10 L310 10' stroke='black'/><circle cx='150' cy='100' r='20' fill='blue'/></svg>

options.text: Paul was rebuked by Elymas
Elymas was struck blind by Paul
Paul and Elymas became allies
Elymas converted to Christianity

questions.explanation: According to Acts 13:4-12, Paul encountered Elymas the magician on Cyprus and rebuked him for opposing the Gospel. As a result, Elymas was struck blind. This event demonstrated Paul's authority and the power of the Gospel.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 9:1-8, Jesus heals a paralytic man. What is Jesus' initial response to the man?

options.text: Your sins are forgiven
Take up your bed and walk
You are healed
Follow me

questions.explanation: In Matthew 9:1-8, Jesus first says to the paralytic man, 'Your sins are forgiven.' This response addresses the spiritual need of the man before his physical healing, demonstrating Jesus' authority to forgive sins.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.subtopic: Pentecost and the Early Christian Community
questions.question_text: According to Acts 2:1-47, what event occurred on the day of Pentecost?

options.text: The apostles were dispersed
The Holy Spirit descended upon the apostles
Peter denied Jesus
The early Christians were persecuted

questions.explanation: On the day of Pentecost, as described in Acts 2:1-47, the Holy Spirit descended upon the apostles, giving them the ability to speak in different languages and marking the beginning of the Church's mission.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 9:27-31, Jesus heals two blind men. What is Jesus' initial instruction to them after the healing?

options.text: To tell everyone about the miracle
To go and sin no more
To see that no one knows about it
To follow Him to the temple

questions.explanation: Jesus heals the two blind men and instructs them to tell no one about the miracle, demonstrating His desire for humility and avoiding unnecessary attention.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.question_text: According to Acts 22:1-21, what is Paul's testimony regarding his conversion experience?

options.text: He was persecuting Christians unknowingly
He was on his way to Damascus to arrest Christians when he encountered Jesus
He was a Roman soldier who converted to Christianity
He was a disciple of Jesus during His ministry

questions.explanation: Paul testifies that he was on his way to Damascus to persecute Christians when he had a dramatic encounter with Jesus, leading to his conversion.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: In Amos 4:1-3, what is the main accusation against the women of Samaria?

options.text: They were neglecting their family duties
They were oppressing the poor and crushing the needy
They were worshipping idols
They were ignoring the Sabbath laws

questions.explanation: Amos condemns the women of Samaria for their role in oppressing the poor and needy, highlighting their social injustice.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.subtopic: Sermon on the Mount and Parables
questions.question_text: In the Parable of the Lost Sheep (Matthew 18:12-14), what does the shepherd's action represent?
questions.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='10' width='300' height='180' fill='#f0f0f0'/><path d='M50,100 Q120,50 200,100' stroke='black' stroke-width='2' fill='none'/><circle cx='50' cy='100' r='10' fill='black'/><circle cx='200' cy='100' r='10' fill='black'/></svg>

options.text: God's justice towards sinners
The value of one soul to God
The importance of community prayer
The danger of straying from the path

questions.explanation: The parable illustrates God's joy and value for each individual soul, represented by the shepherd's efforts to find the one lost sheep.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.subtopic: Pentecost and the Early Christian Community
questions.question_text: According to Acts 4:32-37, what characterizes the early Christian community?

options.text: They were divided over doctrinal issues
They were united in spirit and shared their possessions
They were focused solely on missionary work
They were in constant conflict with the Jewish leaders

questions.explanation: The early Christians were characterized by their unity and generosity, sharing their possessions to meet each other's needs.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 9:32-34, Jesus heals a man who was demon-possessed and mute. What was the reaction of the Pharisees to this miracle?

options.text: They praised Jesus for His divine power.
They attributed Jesus' power to the prince of demons.
They were indifferent to the miracle.
They asked for a sign from Jesus.

questions.explanation: According to Matthew 9:32-34, after Jesus heals a man who was demon-possessed and mute, the Pharisees react by attributing Jesus' power to the prince of demons, indicating their skepticism and hostility towards Jesus' divine authority.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: In Amos 4:1-3, what is the primary accusation made against the 'cows of Bashan'?

options.text: They were worshiping idols.
They were oppressing the poor and needy.
They were neglecting their religious duties.
They were disobedient to their husbands.

questions.explanation: In Amos 4:1-3, the 'cows of Bashan' (referring to the wealthy women of Samaria) are accused primarily of oppressing the poor and needy, highlighting their social injustice and exploitation.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.question_text: According to Acts 22:1-21, what is Paul's testimony regarding his conversion experience?

options.text: He was a willing participant in persecuting Christians.
He was converted while on the road to Damascus.
He received his commission directly from Jesus.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Paul's testimony in Acts 22:1-21 includes being a willing participant in persecuting Christians (Acts 22:4-5), being converted while on the road to Damascus (Acts 22:6-11), and receiving his commission directly from Jesus (Acts 22:14-16, 21). Thus, all the statements are accurate according to his testimony.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.subtopic: Sermon on the Mount and Parables
questions.question_text: In the Parable of the Lost Sheep (Matthew 18:12-14), what does the shepherd's action represent?

options.text: God's judgment on sinners.
The value of each individual to God.
The necessity of following the law strictly.
The importance of community over individual salvation.

questions.explanation: The Parable of the Lost Sheep illustrates God's concern and joy in recovering what is lost, representing the value of each individual to God. Jesus teaches that there is joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, highlighting the importance of individual salvation.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.subtopic: Pentecost and the Early Christian Community
questions.question_text: According to Acts 4:32-37, what characterizes the early Christian community?

options.text: They were divided in their beliefs.
They were united in spirit and purpose.
They were primarily concerned with material wealth.
They were isolated from the rest of the community.

questions.explanation: Acts 4:32-37 describes the early Christian community as being united in spirit and purpose, having one heart and soul, and sharing their possessions to meet the needs of others, demonstrating their unity and generosity.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 9:20-22, a woman with a bleeding disorder touches Jesus' garment. What is Jesus' response to the woman after she touches him?

options.text: He ignores her and continues on his way.
He rebukes her for touching him.
He turns and says, 'Daughter, your faith has made you well.'
He asks who touched him.

questions.explanation: Jesus notices the woman's faith and responds positively, saying, 'Daughter, your faith has made you well.' This demonstrates Jesus' awareness of the miracle and his affirmation of the woman's faith.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: In Amos 5:21-24, what is Amos' attitude towards the religious practices of Israel?

options.text: He praises their sacrifices and festivals.
He is indifferent to their religious practices.
He condemns their empty religious practices, calling for justice.
He suggests they increase their offerings.

questions.explanation: Amos criticizes the Israelites for their hypocritical worship, emphasizing that God desires justice and righteousness rather than mere religious rituals.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.question_text: According to Acts 9:1-31, what is the immediate result of Paul's conversion on the road to Damascus?
questions.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><path d='M50,100 L270,100' stroke='black' stroke-width='2'/><circle cx='50' cx='100' r='10' fill='black'/><text x='55' y='105'>Damascus</text><text x='265' y='105'>Jerusalem</text></svg>

options.text: He immediately begins his missionary journey.
He is blinded and stays in Damascus.
He returns to Jerusalem to resume persecuting Christians.
He is arrested by the Roman authorities.

questions.explanation: After his conversion, Paul is blinded and goes to Damascus, where he is healed and baptized by Ananias, marking the beginning of his transformation into a Christian missionary.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.subtopic: Sermon on the Mount and Parables
questions.question_text: In the Parable of the Mustard Seed (Matthew 13:31-32), what does Jesus compare the Kingdom of Heaven to?

options.text: A treasure hidden in a field.
A mustard seed that grows into a large tree.
A lost sheep that is found.
A servant who is forgiven a debt.

questions.explanation: Jesus uses the mustard seed as a metaphor for the Kingdom of Heaven, illustrating how something small can grow into something significant.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.subtopic: Pentecost and the Early Christian Community
questions.question_text: According to Acts 2:1-47, what event occurred on the day of Pentecost?

options.text: The apostles hid in fear.
The Holy Spirit descended upon the apostles, and they spoke in different tongues.
Paul preached his first sermon.
The early Christians dispersed.

questions.explanation: On the day of Pentecost, the Holy Spirit descended upon the apostles, enabling them to speak in various languages, which was a pivotal moment in the establishment of the early Christian church.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.subtopic: Sermon on the Mount and Parables
questions.question_text: In the Parable of the Sower (Matthew 13:1-23), what does the seed represent?

options.text: The Kingdom of Heaven
The Word of God
The disciples of Jesus
The people of Israel

questions.explanation: In the Parable of the Sower, Jesus explains that the seed represents the Word of God. This is evident from Matthew 13:19, where Jesus says, 'When anyone hears the message about the kingdom and does not understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away what was sown in their heart.' Thus, the seed symbolizes the message or Word of God being spread.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: According to Joshua 24:1-28, what is Joshua's final challenge to the Israelites?

options.text: To continue worshiping the God of their ancestors
To build the Temple in Jerusalem
To serve the Lord and choose this day whom they will serve
To go to war with the remaining Canaanites

questions.explanation: In Joshua 24:15, Joshua challenges the Israelites, saying, 'But if serving the Lord seems undesirable to you, then choose for yourselves this day whom you will serve.' This emphasizes their commitment to serving the Lord, highlighting the importance of their choice.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.question_text: In the diagram below, a map illustrates Paul's third missionary journey. In the context of Acts 18:23-28, what is the significance of Apollos' ministry in Ephesus?
questions.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><path d='M10 10 L100 100' stroke='black'/></svg>

options.text: He preached about Jesus, knowing only the baptism of John
He was a major leader in the church at Corinth
He was sent by Paul to Corinth
He opposed Paul's teachings

questions.explanation: According to Acts 18:25, Apollos 'had been instructed in the way of the Lord; and he spoke with great fervor and taught about Jesus accurately, though he knew only the baptism of John.' This indicates that Apollos' ministry was significant as he preached about Jesus, despite knowing only the baptism of John.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 14:22-33, what is the significance of Jesus walking on water?

options.text: It demonstrated Jesus' power over nature
It was a sign of Jesus' resurrection
It showed Jesus' ability to defy the laws of physics
It was a test of the disciples' faith

questions.explanation: Jesus walking on water, as described in Matthew 14:22-33, demonstrates Jesus' power over nature. This miracle is a testament to Jesus' divine authority and control over the natural world, reinforcing the disciples' faith and understanding of Jesus' identity.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: According to Amos 5:21-24, what is Amos' attitude towards the religious practices of Israel?

options.text: He is pleased with their festivals and sacrifices
He is indifferent to their religious practices
He rejects their festivals and desires justice to flow like a river
He suggests they increase their offerings

questions.explanation: In Amos 5:21-24, Amos expresses his displeasure with the religious practices of Israel, stating that he hates and despises their religious festivals and will not accept their burnt offerings and grain offerings. Instead, he desires justice to roll down like a river and righteousness like a never-failing stream.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.subtopic: Sermon on the Mount and Parables
questions.question_text: In the Parable of the Sower (Matthew 13:1-23), what does the seed that fell on rocky ground represent?

options.text: Those who hear the word and immediately receive it with joy
Those who hear the word but are choked by the worries of this life
Those who hear the word and understand it, then produce fruit
Those who hear the word but do not understand it

questions.explanation: The Parable of the Sower explains different responses to the message of the Kingdom. The seed on rocky ground represents those who receive the word with joy but lack depth, causing it to wither. This is described in Matthew 13:20-21.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: According to Joshua 6:1-27, what was the strategy used by Joshua to capture Jericho?
questions.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='50' y='50' width='220' height='100' fill='none' stroke='black'/><text x='160' y='120' text-anchor='middle'>Jericho</text></svg>

options.text: The Israelites marched around the city once and then attacked
The Israelites marched around the city seven times and then shouted
The Israelites built a siege ramp around the city
The Israelites bribed the city's guards to surrender

questions.explanation: Joshua 6:1-27 describes how the Israelites marched around Jericho once a day for six days and on the seventh day, they circled the city seven times. On the seventh circuit, they shouted, and the walls collapsed.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 14:13-21, what miracle did Jesus perform when a large crowd followed him to a remote area?

options.text: Healing a blind man
Feeding the 5,000 with five loaves and two fish
Raising a dead person
Calming a storm

questions.explanation: Matthew 14:13-21 describes Jesus feeding the 5,000 with five loaves of bread and two fish, demonstrating his miraculous provision for the crowd.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.question_text: According to Acts 9:1-31, what was the immediate result of Paul's conversion on the road to Damascus?

options.text: He immediately began preaching in Damascus
He was struck blind and had to be led into the city
He escaped from Damascus to Jerusalem
He was baptized by Ananias and regained his sight

questions.explanation: Acts 9:1-31 describes Paul's conversion experience where he was struck blind. After being led into Damascus, he was baptized by Ananias and regained his sight.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: In Amos 5:21-24, what is Amos' attitude towards the religious practices of Israel?

options.text: He praised their faithfulness and rituals
He was neutral, neither praising nor condemning
He condemned their empty rituals and called for justice
He ignored their practices and focused on other issues

questions.explanation: Amos 5:21-24 shows Amos rejecting Israel's religious festivals and offerings because they lacked justice and righteousness. He called for a genuine expression of faith.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.subtopic: Sermon on the Mount and Parables
questions.question_text: In the context of the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5-7), what is Jesus' teaching on the subject of anxiety, as recorded in Matthew 6:25-34?

options.text: Jesus instructs his followers to worry about their daily needs.
Jesus teaches that anxiety is a sign of faith.
Jesus advises his followers not to worry about tomorrow, for today has enough trouble of its own.
Jesus commands his followers to prioritize material wealth above all else.

questions.explanation: Jesus teaches that his followers should not worry about tomorrow because today has enough trouble of its own (Matthew 6:34). This instruction is part of a larger discourse where Jesus encourages trust in God's provision, using the examples of birds and lilies to illustrate how God cares for his creation. The correct answer reflects Jesus' teaching on not being anxious about daily needs.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: According to Amos 5:21-24, what is Amos' attitude towards the religious practices of Israel?

options.text: Amos is pleased with their religious practices.
Amos is indifferent to their religious practices.
Amos rejects their religious practices, calling for justice to roll down like waters.
Amos suggests that their religious practices are sufficient for their salvation.

questions.explanation: Amos expresses a negative attitude towards the religious practices of Israel, stating that he hates and despises their religious festivals and will not delight in their solemn assemblies. Instead, he calls for justice to roll down like waters and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream (Amos 5:24). This indicates that Amos values justice and righteousness over ritual observance.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.question_text: In the diagram below, a map illustrates Paul's second missionary journey. In the context of Acts 16:9-10, what is the significance of the vision Paul received in Troas? In the diagram below, ...
questions.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='10' width='300' height='180' fill='#f0f0f0'/><text x='160' y='100' text-anchor='middle'>Map of Paul's 2nd journey</text></svg>

options.text: The vision instructed Paul to return to Jerusalem.
The vision commanded Paul to go to Macedonia and help them.
The vision told Paul to preach to the Gentiles in Asia Minor.
The vision advised Paul to stay in Troas.

questions.explanation: According to Acts 16:9-10, Paul received a vision of a man from Macedonia calling for help. This vision was a divine directive for Paul to cross over into Macedonia and assist them, marking a significant turning point in his missionary journey as it led him to Europe.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 9:20-22, a woman with a bleeding disorder touches Jesus' garment. What is Jesus' response to the woman?

options.text: Jesus rebukes the woman for touching him.
Jesus ignores the woman.
Jesus says, 'Your faith has healed you.'
Jesus asks who touched him but does not respond further.

questions.explanation: Jesus responds to the woman by acknowledging her faith, saying, 'Your faith has healed you.' This response not only heals her physically but also commends her faith, highlighting the significance of faith in Jesus' ministry.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.subtopic: Pentecost and the Early Christian Community
questions.question_text: According to Acts 2:1-47, what event occurred on the day of Pentecost?

options.text: The disciples scattered due to persecution.
The Holy Spirit descended upon the disciples, and they spoke in various tongues.
The apostles elected new leaders for the church.
The early Christians decided to abandon their mission.

questions.explanation: On the day of Pentecost, the Holy Spirit descended upon the disciples, empowering them to speak in various tongues, thus enabling them to communicate the message of Jesus Christ to people from different linguistic backgrounds. This event marked the beginning of the church's mission to spread the gospel.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 9:1-8, Jesus heals a paralytic man. What is Jesus' initial response to the man?

options.text: Take up your bed and walk
Follow me
Your sins are forgiven
Go and sin no more

questions.explanation: Jesus first addresses the man's spiritual need by saying 'Your sins are forgiven.' This response highlights Jesus' authority to forgive sins, which was a controversial aspect of his ministry.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: According to Amos 5:18-20, what is Amos' message to those who desire the day of the Lord?

options.text: It will be a day of joy and celebration
It will be a day of darkness and not light
It will be a day of rest and worship
It will be a day of war and conquest

questions.explanation: Amos warns that the day of the Lord will be a day of darkness and not light, indicating judgment rather than salvation for those who are unrepentant.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.question_text: In the diagram below, a map illustrates Paul's first missionary journey. In the context of Acts 13:4-12, what is the significance of Paul's ministry in Cyprus? <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='10' width='300' height='180' fill='#f0f0f0'/><text x='160' y='100' text-anchor='middle'>Map of Cyprus</text></svg>
questions.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='10' width='300' height='180' fill='#f0f0f0'/><text x='160' y='100' text-anchor='middle'>Map of Cyprus</text></svg>

options.text: Paul was rejected by the proconsul
Paul healed a crippled man and confronted a false prophet
Paul only preached to Jews
Paul established no churches

questions.explanation: Paul's ministry in Cyprus included healing a crippled man and confronting a false prophet, Elymas, demonstrating God's power and Paul's authority.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.subtopic: Sermon on the Mount and Parables
questions.question_text: In the context of the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5-7), what is Jesus' teaching on the subject of loving one's neighbors?

options.text: Love your neighbor and hate your enemy
Love your neighbor as yourself
Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you
Only love those who love you

questions.explanation: Jesus teaches to love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, extending the concept of loving one's neighbors to include even those who are hostile.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.subtopic: Pentecost and the Early Christian Community
questions.question_text: According to Acts 2:1-47, what is the result of Peter's sermon on the day of Pentecost?

options.text: About 3,000 people were baptized
The crowd was hostile and dispersed
Peter was arrested by the authorities
The disciples fled in fear

questions.explanation: Peter's sermon on the day of Pentecost resulted in about 3,000 people being baptized, marking a significant growth in the early Christian community.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 9:1-8, Jesus heals a paralytic man. What is Jesus' initial response to the man?

options.text: Your sins are forgiven
Rise and walk
Follow me
Go and sin no more

questions.explanation: Jesus first addresses the man's spiritual need by saying 'Your sins are forgiven', before healing him physically by saying 'Rise and walk'. This demonstrates Jesus' authority to forgive sins.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.question_text: According to Acts 9:1-31, what was the immediate result of Paul's conversion on the road to Damascus?

options.text: He immediately began preaching about Jesus
He was blinded and had to be led into Damascus
He was baptized by Ananias
He escaped from Damascus to Jerusalem

questions.explanation: Upon encountering the risen Jesus on the road to Damascus, Paul was blinded by a bright light and had to be led into the city, where he was subsequently healed and baptized by Ananias.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: In Amos 5:21-24, what is Amos' attitude towards the religious practices of Israel?

options.text: He is pleased with their sincerity
He is indifferent to their practices
He rejects their empty religious rituals
He commands them to continue their current practices

questions.explanation: Amos criticizes the Israelites for their hypocritical worship, indicating that God desires justice and righteousness rather than empty religious rituals.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.subtopic: Sermon on the Mount and Parables
questions.question_text: In the Parable of the Sower (Matthew 13:1-23), what does the seed represent?
questions.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='10' width='300' height='180' fill='#f0f0f0'/><path d='M 50,100 L 270,100' stroke='black' stroke-width='2'/><circle cx='60' cy='100' r='10' fill='black'/><circle cx='120' cy='100' r='10' fill='black'/><circle cx='180' cy='100' r='10' fill='black'/><circle cx='240' cy='100' r='10' fill='black'/></svg>

options.text: The people listening to Jesus
The message of the Kingdom
The disciples of Jesus
The Pharisees and Sadducees

questions.explanation: The seed in the Parable of the Sower represents the message of the Kingdom of God. The different types of soil represent various responses to this message.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.subtopic: Pentecost and the Early Christian Community
questions.question_text: According to Acts 2:1-47, what event occurred on the day of Pentecost?

options.text: The apostles were scattered throughout Jerusalem
The Holy Spirit descended upon the apostles
Peter denied Jesus for the third time
The Pharisees interrogated the apostles

questions.explanation: On the day of Pentecost, the Holy Spirit descended upon the apostles, giving them the ability to speak in different languages and empowering them to preach about Jesus to the gathered crowd.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 9:32-34, what miracle did Jesus perform on a man who was demon-possessed and unable to speak?

options.text: He healed the man's physical blindness.
He cast out the demon, and the man spoke.
He raised the man from the dead.
He fed the man with miraculous food.

questions.explanation: According to Matthew 9:32-34, Jesus cast out a demon from a man who was unable to speak, and subsequently, the man was able to speak. This miracle is a demonstration of Jesus' authority over unclean spirits.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: According to Joshua 8:1-29, what was the strategy used by Joshua to capture Ai?
questions.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='50' y='50' width='100' height='50' fill='#ccc'/><text x='75' y='75' font-size='12'>Ai</text></svg>

options.text: Joshua directly attacked Ai with his entire army.
Joshua used an ambush strategy, setting a trap behind the city.
Joshua sent spies to gather information before attacking.
Joshua waited for Ai to surrender peacefully.

questions.explanation: Joshua 8:1-29 describes how Joshua used an ambush strategy to capture Ai. He set a group of warriors in ambush behind the city, while he and the rest of the army pretended to retreat. The people of Ai pursued them, leaving the city undefended, and the ambush group then attacked and captured the city.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.question_text: In the context of Acts 16:9-10, what is the significance of the Macedonian call to Paul?
questions.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><path d='M50,50 L150,150' stroke='#000' stroke-width='2'/><text x='100' y='100' font-size='12'>Macedonia</text></svg>

options.text: It marked the end of Paul's missionary journeys.
It signified Paul's call to preach to the Gentiles.
It led Paul to change his missionary plans and head to Macedonia.
It resulted in Paul's imprisonment.

questions.explanation: Acts 16:9-10 describes Paul's vision of a man from Macedonia calling for help. This vision led Paul to change his missionary plans and travel to Macedonia, marking a significant shift in his missionary work.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.subtopic: Sermon on the Mount and Parables
questions.question_text: In the context of the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5-7), what is Jesus' teaching on the subject of prayer, as recorded in the Lord's Prayer?

options.text: Jesus taught his disciples to pray for revenge on their enemies.
Jesus instructed his disciples to pray for daily bread and forgiveness.
Jesus emphasized the importance of lengthy and repetitive prayers.
Jesus discouraged his disciples from praying altogether.

questions.explanation: The Lord's Prayer, as recorded in Matthew 6:9-13, includes petitions for daily bread and forgiveness, among other things. Jesus taught his disciples to pray sincerely and concisely, focusing on essential matters.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: According to Amos 5:18-20, what is Amos' message to those who desire the day of the Lord?

options.text: Amos welcomes the day of the Lord as a time of joy and celebration.
Amos is neutral about the day of the Lord, leaving its interpretation open.
Amos warns that the day of the Lord will be darkness and not light.
Amos postpones the day of the Lord to a future date.

questions.explanation: Amos 5:18-20 conveys Amos' warning that the day of the Lord will be a time of darkness and judgment, not light and joy, for those who have not lived righteously.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.subtopic: Sermon on the Mount and Parables
questions.question_text: In the context of the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5-7), what is Jesus' teaching on the subject of hypocrisy, as recorded in Matthew 6:2-18?

options.text: Jesus encourages his followers to practice their religious duties in secret to avoid being seen by others.
Jesus teaches that giving to the needy should be done publicly to set an example for others.
Jesus advises his followers to pray in public so that they may be heard by God.
Jesus instructs his followers to fast and make it obvious to others so that they may be recognized as devout.

questions.explanation: Jesus teaches that acts of righteousness such as giving to the needy (Matthew 6:2-4), praying (Matthew 6:5-6), and fasting (Matthew 6:16-18) should be done in secret. The Father who sees in secret will reward them. This emphasizes the importance of sincerity and avoiding hypocrisy.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: According to Amos 7:1-9:15, what is the significance of the visions received by Amos?

options.text: The visions foretell the coming prosperity and peace of Israel.
The visions are a call to repentance and a warning of impending judgment on Israel due to their sins.
The visions predict the downfall of Judah but not Israel.
The visions are primarily about the restoration of the Davidic kingdom.

questions.explanation: Amos receives a series of visions from God, which include locusts, fire, a plumb line, a basket of summer fruit, and the Lord standing by a wall with a plumb line (Amos 7:1-9, 8:1-3, 9:1). These visions symbolize God's judgment on Israel for their sins and serve as a call to repentance. The visions emphasize God's justice and the inevitability of judgment if Israel does not turn from their wicked ways.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.question_text: In the diagram below, a map illustrates Paul's second missionary journey. In the context of Acts 16:9-10, what is the significance of the Macedonian call to Paul? <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='10' width='300' height='180' fill='none' stroke='black'/><path d='M50,50 L270,50' stroke='black'/><text x='160' y='40' font-size='12'>Macedonian Call</text></svg>
questions.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='10' width='300' height='180' fill='none' stroke='black'/><path d='M50,50 L270,50' stroke='black'/><text x='160' y='40' font-size='12'>Macedonian Call</text></svg>

options.text: The Macedonian call was a vision Paul received to preach the gospel in Asia Minor.
The Macedonian call was a divine invitation for Paul to enter Macedonia and preach the gospel.
The Macedonian call signified the end of Paul's missionary journeys.
The Macedonian call was a command for Paul to return to Jerusalem.

questions.explanation: According to Acts 16:9-10, Paul had a vision of a man from Macedonia pleading with him to come and help them. This vision was interpreted by Paul and his companions as a call from God to preach the gospel in Macedonia. The Macedonian call marked a significant turning point in Paul's second missionary journey, as it led him to cross into Europe and establish churches in places like Philippi.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 9:20-22, a woman with a bleeding disorder touches Jesus' garment. What is Jesus' response to the woman?

options.text: Jesus rebukes the woman for touching him.
Jesus ignores the woman and continues on his way.
Jesus says, 'Your faith has healed you,' and the woman is made well from that moment.
Jesus asks the woman to come forward and explain why she touched him, but does not heal her.

questions.explanation: When the woman with a bleeding disorder touches Jesus' garment, Jesus feels that power has gone out from him. He turns and sees the woman, and says, 'Take heart, daughter; your faith has healed you.' The woman is made well from that moment, indicating that Jesus attributes her healing to her faith.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.subtopic: Pentecost and the Early Christian Community
questions.question_text: According to Acts 2:1-47, what is the result of Peter's sermon on the day of Pentecost?

options.text: About 3,000 people are convicted of sin but do not believe.
Peter's sermon is met with hostility and rejection by the crowd.
Approximately 3,000 people believe and are baptized, becoming part of the early Christian community.
The sermon has no significant impact on the listeners.

questions.explanation: On the day of Pentecost, Peter preaches a sermon explaining the phenomenon of speaking in tongues as a fulfillment of Joel's prophecy and proclaiming Jesus as Lord and Christ. The sermon convicts the listeners, and about 3,000 people believe and are baptized, becoming part of the early Christian community. This event marks the beginning of the church and demonstrates the powerful impact of the gospel message.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 8:23-27, what miracle did Jesus perform when a storm arose on the Sea of Galilee?

options.text: He walked on water
He calmed the storm
He fed a multitude
He healed a blind man

questions.explanation: In Matthew 8:23-27, Jesus calmed the storm on the Sea of Galilee. The disciples, who were frightened by the storm, woke Jesus and He rebuked the winds and the sea, resulting in a great calm. This miracle demonstrates Jesus' authority over nature.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: In the context of Joshua 10:1-14, what miraculous event occurred during the battle against the five Amorite kings?

options.text: The sun stood still
The Jordan River parted again
The walls of Jericho fell
The Israelites were defeated

questions.explanation: In Joshua 10:1-14, Joshua prayed for the sun and moon to stand still during the battle against the five Amorite kings, allowing the Israelites to achieve victory. The sun stood still in the midst of heaven and did not hasten to go down for about a whole day.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.question_text: According to Acts 13:4-12, what was the outcome of Paul's preaching in the synagogue at Salamis on his first missionary journey?
questions.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='10' width='300' height='180' fill='#f0f0f0'/><text x='160' y='100' text-anchor='middle'>Map of Paul's First Missionary Journey</text></svg>

options.text: He was rejected by the Jews
He was welcomed by the proconsul
He preached to the Gentiles only
He performed a miracle on a crippled man

questions.explanation: In Acts 13:4-12, Paul and Barnabas preached in the synagogues of Salamis. Later, in Paphos, Paul confronted Elymas, a sorcerer, and struck him with blindness, which led to the conversion of Sergius Paulus, the proconsul. The correct interpretation involves understanding the broader context of Paul's ministry in Cyprus.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.subtopic: Sermon on the Mount and Parables
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 7:7-8, what is Jesus' teaching on prayer?

options.text: Ask and it will be given to you; seek and you will find; knock and the door will be opened to you
Pray only for your own needs
Prayer is not necessary for Christians
Only pray on special occasions

questions.explanation: In Matthew 7:7-8, Jesus teaches that persistent prayer is encouraged. He says to 'Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.' This emphasizes the importance of seeking God actively and persistently in prayer.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.subtopic: Pentecost and the Early Christian Community
questions.question_text: According to Acts 2:42-47, what characterized the daily life of the early Christian community?

options.text: They devoted themselves to prayer and fellowship
They focused solely on accumulating wealth
They were isolated from one another
They rejected the apostles' teachings

questions.explanation: In Acts 2:42-47, the early Christian community is described as devoting themselves to the apostles' teaching, fellowship, breaking bread, and prayer. They shared their possessions and met each other's needs, demonstrating a strong sense of community and unity.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 14:22-33, what miracle did Jesus perform when he walked on the water?

options.text: He calmed the storm
He fed the multitude
He saved Peter from drowning
He turned water into wine

questions.explanation: In Matthew 14:22-33, Jesus performed the miracle of saving Peter from drowning when Peter attempted to walk on water towards Jesus. Jesus rebuked Peter for his lack of faith, saying, 'You of little faith, why did you doubt?' The correct answer is C, as it directly relates to the event described.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: According to Joshua 6:1-27, what was the strategy used by Joshua to capture Jericho?
questions.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='50' y='50' width='100' height='50' fill='#ccc'/><text x='100' y='75' font-size='24'>Jericho</text></svg>

options.text: Marching around the city once
Marching around the city seven times
Launching a direct attack on the city gates
Using siege engines to breach the walls

questions.explanation: The biblical account in Joshua 6:1-27 describes how Joshua and the Israelites captured Jericho by marching around the city seven times, following the instructions given by God. On the seventh day, after circling the city seven times, the priests blew their trumpets, and the people shouted, causing the walls to collapse. Thus, the correct answer is B.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.question_text: According to Acts 9:1-31, what was the immediate result of Paul's conversion on the road to Damascus?

options.text: He immediately began preaching in Damascus
He was blinded and taken into Damascus
He escaped from Damascus
He went directly to Jerusalem

questions.explanation: Acts 9:1-31 records that as a result of Paul's conversion on the road to Damascus, he was blinded by a bright light and subsequently taken into Damascus by those who accompanied him, as he was unable to see. The correct answer is B, as it accurately describes the immediate outcome of Paul's conversion experience.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.subtopic: Sermon on the Mount and Parables
questions.question_text: In the Parable of the Sower (Matthew 13:1-23), what does the seed represent?

options.text: The people who hear the message
The message of the kingdom
The disciples of Jesus
The Pharisees and Sadducees

questions.explanation: In the Parable of the Sower, Jesus explains that the seed represents the message of the kingdom of God. The different types of soil represent various responses to this message. Thus, the correct interpretation is that the seed symbolizes the word or message being preached.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.subtopic: Pentecost and the Early Christian Community
questions.question_text: According to Acts 2:42-47, what characterized the daily life of the early Christian community?

options.text: They devoted themselves to prayer and fellowship
They focused solely on preaching to outsiders
They were primarily concerned with material wealth
They were divided into factions

questions.explanation: Acts 2:42-47 describes the early Christian community as being devoted to the apostles' teaching, fellowship, breaking bread, and prayer. They shared their possessions and met each other's needs, demonstrating a strong sense of unity and communal life. The correct answer is A, as it accurately reflects the characteristics of their daily life.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 14:22-33, what miracle did Jesus perform when he walked on the water?

options.text: He calmed the storm
He fed the multitude
He walked on the water
He healed the blind men

questions.explanation: In Matthew 14:22-33, Jesus performed the miracle of walking on the water. This event demonstrates Jesus' power over nature and his ability to reassure his disciples in times of fear and doubt.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: According to Joshua 8:1-29, what was the strategy used by Joshua to capture Ai?
questions.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='10' width='50' height='30' fill='#ccc'/><text x='20' y='25'>Ai</text></svg>

options.text: Direct frontal assault
Ambush and surprise attack
Siege warfare
Negotiation and surrender

questions.explanation: Joshua 8:1-29 describes the strategy used to capture Ai as an ambush and surprise attack. Joshua instructed a group of warriors to lie in ambush behind the city, while he and the main body of troops pretended to retreat. When the men of Ai pursued them, the ambush party attacked the city, and Joshua's forces turned back to defeat Ai.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.question_text: According to Acts 9:1-31, what was the immediate result of Paul's conversion on the road to Damascus?

options.text: He immediately began preaching in Damascus
He was blinded and stayed in Damascus for several days
He escaped from Damascus to Jerusalem
He was arrested by the Roman authorities

questions.explanation: Acts 9:1-31 records that after Paul's conversion on the road to Damascus, he was blinded and stayed in Damascus for several days. During this time, he did not eat or drink, and was visited by Ananias who restored his sight and baptized him.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.subtopic: Sermon on the Mount and Parables
questions.question_text: In the Parable of the Sower (Matthew 13:1-23), what does the seed represent?

options.text: The people who hear the word
The word of God
The kingdom of heaven
The disciples of Jesus

questions.explanation: In the Parable of the Sower (Matthew 13:1-23), Jesus explains that the seed represents the word of God. The different types of soil represent the various responses to the word.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.subtopic: Pentecost and the Early Christian Community
questions.question_text: According to Acts 2:42-47, what characterized the daily life of the early Christian community?

options.text: They were primarily focused on missionary work
They devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and fellowship
They were mainly concerned with resolving internal conflicts
They spent most of their time in prayer and fasting

questions.explanation: Acts 2:42-47 describes the daily life of the early Christian community as being devoted to the apostles' teaching, fellowship, breaking bread, and prayer. They shared their possessions and met each other's needs, demonstrating a strong sense of unity and care for one another.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 9:18-26, a woman with a bleeding disorder touches Jesus' garment, and a ruler's daughter is raised from the dead. What is the common theme between these two miracles?

options.text: Jesus' authority over nature
The importance of faith in Jesus' ministry
Jesus' power over demons
The role of prayer in Jesus' miracles

questions.explanation: Both miracles highlight the significance of faith. The woman with a bleeding disorder is healed because of her faith (Matthew 9:22), and the ruler's daughter is raised after Jesus assures the ruler that his daughter will be well if he has faith (Matthew 9:22, 29). The common theme is the importance of faith in Jesus' ministry.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: According to Amos 4:1-3, what is the main criticism Amos has towards the women of Samaria?

options.text: Their idolatry
Their oppression of the poor
Their immoral behavior
Their lack of faith

questions.explanation: Amos 4:1-3 criticizes the women of Samaria, referred to as 'cows of Bashan,' for their role in oppressing the poor and their luxurious lifestyle at the expense of the needy.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.question_text: In the diagram below, a map illustrates Paul's first missionary journey. In the context of Acts 13:4-14:28, what is the significance of the locations visited during this journey? <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='10' width='300' height='180' fill='#ccc'/><path d='M 50 50 L 270 150' stroke='black'/></svg>
questions.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='10' width='300' height='180' fill='#ccc'/><path d='M 50 50 L 270 150' stroke='black'/></svg>

options.text: They were primarily Gentile cities
They were all Jewish synagogues
They represented a strategic outreach to both Jews and Gentiles
They were chosen randomly

questions.explanation: Paul's first missionary journey, as recorded in Acts 13:4-14:28, involved visiting locations that were strategically chosen to reach both Jewish and Gentile audiences, reflecting the early Christian mission to spread the Gospel to various groups.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.subtopic: Sermon on the Mount and Parables
questions.question_text: In the context of the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5-7), what is Jesus' teaching on the subject of love for one's enemies, as recorded in Matthew 5:43-48?

options.text: To hate them as they hate you
To love them as you love your neighbors
To love them and pray for those who persecute you
To ignore them completely

questions.explanation: Jesus teaches that one should love their enemies and pray for those who persecute them (Matthew 5:44), emphasizing a higher standard of love that goes beyond conventional boundaries.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.subtopic: Pentecost and the Early Christian Community
questions.question_text: According to Acts 2:14-41, what is the central message of Peter's sermon on the day of Pentecost?

options.text: The coming of the Holy Spirit
The resurrection and exaltation of Jesus Christ
The importance of baptism
The unity of the early Christian community

questions.explanation: Peter's sermon on the day of Pentecost, as recorded in Acts 2:14-41, centers on the resurrection and exaltation of Jesus Christ, using Psalm 16 and other scriptures to demonstrate that Jesus is the Messiah.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: According to Amos 3:1-2, what is the main accusation Amos makes against Israel?

options.text: Idolatry and false worship
Social injustice and oppression of the poor
Failure to keep the covenant with God
Rejection of the prophets' messages

questions.explanation: Amos 3:1-2 states that God has known Israel above all the families of the earth, implying a special relationship and responsibility. The main accusation is Israel's failure to live up to this covenant, making option C the correct answer.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 9:1-8, what miracle did Jesus perform, and what was the response of the crowd?

options.text: He healed a blind man, and the crowd was amazed
He forgave a paralytic man's sins and healed him, and the crowd glorified God
He raised a widow's son from the dead, and the crowd feared God
He cast out a demon, and the crowd was divided

questions.explanation: Matthew 9:1-8 describes Jesus forgiving a paralytic man's sins and then healing him. The crowd's response was to glorify God, making option B the correct answer.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.question_text: According to Acts 22:1-21, what was Paul's testimony regarding his conversion experience?

options.text: He was persecuting Christians until Jesus appeared to him on the road to Damascus
He was a Roman soldier who converted after witnessing a miracle
He was a Pharisee who studied under Gamaliel and became a Christian
He was a Gentile who was converted through the ministry of Peter

questions.explanation: Acts 22:1-21 recounts Paul's testimony of his conversion, where he describes being a persecutor of Christians until Jesus appeared to him on the road to Damascus, making option A the correct answer.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: In the diagram below, a map illustrates the conquest of Canaan under Joshua. In the context of Joshua 6:1-27, what was the strategy used to capture Jericho? <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='10' width='300' height='180' fill='#ccc'/><text x='160' y='100' text-anchor='middle'>Map of Jericho's Conquest</text></svg>
questions.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='10' width='300' height='180' fill='#ccc'/><text x='160' y='100' text-anchor='middle'>Map of Jericho's Conquest</text></svg>

options.text: Direct military assault
Siege and circumambulation around the city
Diplomacy and negotiation
Divine intervention without human action

questions.explanation: Joshua 6:1-27 describes the strategy used to capture Jericho, which involved the Israelites marching around the city, making option B the correct answer.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.subtopic: Sermon on the Mount and Parables
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 5:21-22, what is Jesus' teaching on anger?

options.text: Anger is always justified and righteous
Anger is never justified and is always sinful
Anger can be sinful if it is unjustified or leads to harmful actions
Jesus does not address anger directly

questions.explanation: Matthew 5:21-22 indicates that Jesus teaches anger can be sinful, especially when it involves insulting or demeaning others, making option C the most accurate representation of His teaching.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 9:32-34, what miracle did Jesus perform on a man who was demon-possessed and mute, and what was the response of the Pharisees?

options.text: Jesus healed the man, and the Pharisees praised God.
Jesus cast out the demon, and the Pharisees attributed the miracle to Beelzebul.
Jesus forgave the man's sins, and the Pharisees were silent.
Jesus raised the man from the dead, and the Pharisees were amazed.

questions.explanation: According to Matthew 9:32-34, Jesus cast out a demon from a mute man, and the Pharisees responded by saying Jesus was able to cast out demons because He was empowered by Beelzebul, the prince of demons. This shows their skepticism and accusation towards Jesus' divine authority.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: According to Joshua 24:1-28, what was Joshua's final challenge to the Israelites before his death?

options.text: To continue worshipping the Lord and following His laws.
To go to war with the remaining Canaanite nations.
To build the Temple in Jerusalem.
To establish a monarchy.

questions.explanation: Joshua 24:1-28 records Joshua's farewell address where he challenges the Israelites to remain faithful to the Lord, serve Him alone, and put away the foreign gods among them. This emphasizes the importance of covenant loyalty and obedience to God's laws.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.question_text: In the diagram below, a map illustrates Paul's third missionary journey. In the context of Acts 18:23-21:17, what significant event occurred during this journey? <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='10' width='300' height='180' fill='#ccc'/><path d='M50,50 L270,150' stroke='black' stroke-width='2'/></svg>
questions.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='10' width='300' height='180' fill='#ccc'/><path d='M50,50 L270,150' stroke='black' stroke-width='2'/></svg>

options.text: Paul's conversion on the road to Damascus.
The Council of Jerusalem.
Paul's arrest in Jerusalem and subsequent imprisonment.
The raising of Eutychus in Troas.

questions.explanation: During Paul's third missionary journey, as recorded in Acts 20:7-12, he raised Eutychus from the dead in Troas after the young man fell out of a window during Paul's lengthy sermon. This event is a significant miracle associated with Paul's ministry.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.subtopic: Sermon on the Mount and Parables
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 6:25-34, what is Jesus' teaching on anxiety and worry?

options.text: Jesus teaches that anxiety is a sign of faith.
Jesus instructs His followers not to worry about tomorrow because God provides for the birds and flowers.
Jesus commands His followers to worry about their material needs.
Jesus says that worry is not a concern for Christians.

questions.explanation: In Matthew 6:25-34, Jesus teaches that His followers should not be anxious about their needs because God knows what they need and will provide for them, just as He does for the birds and flowers. This passage encourages trust in God's providence.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.subtopic: Pentecost and the Early Christian Community
questions.question_text: According to Acts 4:32-37, what characterized the possessions and behavior of the early Christian community?

options.text: They held all possessions individually and competed for resources.
They sold their possessions and distributed them according to individual need.
They kept their possessions and only shared their faith.
They gave all their possessions to the apostles to manage.

questions.explanation: Acts 4:32-37 describes the early Christian community as having a shared sense of ownership and generosity, where believers sold their possessions and goods to distribute to those in need, demonstrating unity and care for one another.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 9:20-22, a woman with a bleeding disorder touches Jesus' garment. What was the immediate result of her action?

options.text: She was healed instantly
She felt worse
Jesus was angered
The crowd was displeased

questions.explanation: According to Matthew 9:20-22, when the woman with a bleeding disorder touched Jesus' garment, she was healed instantly. Jesus felt that power had gone out from him, and he turned to her, saying, 'Take heart, daughter; your faith has made you well.' This demonstrates Jesus' power to heal through faith.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: According to Amos 5:21-24, what was Amos' attitude towards the religious practices of Israel?

options.text: He was supportive of their sacrifices and festivals
He was indifferent to their religious practices
He rejected their sacrifices and festivals, calling for justice
He advocated for more frequent sacrifices

questions.explanation: Amos 5:21-24 indicates that Amos rejected the sacrifices and festivals of Israel, stating that God detests their religious festivals and does not delight in their solemn assemblies. Instead, Amos called for justice to roll down like waters and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream, emphasizing the need for ethical behavior over ritual practices.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.question_text: In the diagram below, a map illustrates Paul's second missionary journey. In the context of Acts 15:36-18:22, what significant event occurred during this journey? <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='10' width='300' height='180' fill='#ccc'/><path d='M50,50 L270,150' stroke='black' stroke-width='2'/></svg>
questions.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='10' width='300' height='180' fill='#ccc'/><path d='M50,50 L270,150' stroke='black' stroke-width='2'/></svg>

options.text: Paul met Priscilla and Aquila in Corinth
Paul had a vision of a man from Macedonia calling for help
Paul preached in the Areopagus in Athens
All of the above

questions.explanation: During Paul's second missionary journey (Acts 15:36-18:22), several significant events occurred. Paul met Priscilla and Aquila in Corinth (Acts 18:1-2), had a vision of a man from Macedonia calling for help (Acts 16:9-10), and preached in the Areopagus in Athens (Acts 17:22-34). Thus, all the mentioned events took place during this journey.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.subtopic: Sermon on the Mount and Parables
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 5:38-42, what is Jesus' teaching on retaliation?

options.text: An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth
Resist evil with force
Turn the other cheek and go the extra mile
Seek revenge

questions.explanation: Jesus taught his followers not to retaliate when wronged. Instead, he instructed them to 'turn the other cheek' and 'go the extra mile' (Matthew 5:38-42), promoting a response of non-violence and generosity towards those who mistreat them.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.subtopic: Pentecost and the Early Christian Community
questions.question_text: According to Acts 2:1-4, what miraculous event occurred on the day of Pentecost?

options.text: The disciples were filled with fear
The Holy Spirit descended upon the disciples with tongues of fire
Peter preached a sermon
The crowd dispersed

questions.explanation: On the day of Pentecost, as described in Acts 2:1-4, the Holy Spirit descended upon the disciples. This event was marked by the appearance of tongues of fire that rested on each of them, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, enabling them to speak in different languages.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 9:1-8, what miracle did Jesus perform, and what was the initial response of the Pharisees?

options.text: He healed a paralytic, and they praised God.
He healed a paralytic, and they blasphemed.
He raised a widow's son, and they were afraid.
He cleansed a leper, and they were filled with anger.

questions.explanation: In Matthew 9:1-8, Jesus heals a paralytic man. The Pharisees saw this and thought Jesus was blaspheming because He forgave sins, which they believed only God could do. Thus, the correct answer reflects this event and their negative response.

questions.topic: The Early Church and Paul's Mission
questions.question_text: According to Acts 22:1-21, what was the central aspect of Paul's testimony regarding his conversion experience?

options.text: His persecution of Christians before conversion.
His divine calling to preach to Gentiles.
His miraculous escape from prison.
His role in the stoning of Stephen.

questions.explanation: In Acts 22:1-21, Paul recounts his conversion experience and highlights his calling to preach to the Gentiles as a central aspect of his testimony. This is a key element of his conversion narrative.

questions.topic: Old Testament (Creation to Exile)
questions.question_text: According to Amos 5:21-24, what was Amos' attitude towards the religious practices of Israel?

options.text: He praised their sincerity and faithfulness.
He was indifferent to their practices.
He rejected their religious festivals and offerings.
He encouraged them to continue their rituals.

questions.explanation: Amos 5:21-24 indicates that Amos rejected the religious festivals and offerings of Israel because they were not accompanied by justice and righteousness. He desired justice to roll down like waters.

questions.topic: New Testament (Life and Ministry of Jesus)
questions.subtopic: Sermon on the Mount and Parables
questions.question_text: In the context of Matthew 6:25-34, what is Jesus' teaching on anxiety and worry?

options.text: He encouraged His followers to be anxious about their needs.
He taught that anxiety is a sign of faith.
He instructed His followers not to worry about tomorrow.
He said that worry is necessary for salvation.
